rules.statement: Every code path that sets a local account's password (create, reset, self-service change, seeding) must validate it through the single shared password policy seam before the password is hashed or stored, never accepting any non-empty value or relying on a store's own validators.
rules.why: Stores differ in what they refuse and a custom store would skip their checks, so the verifier owns the rules and a refused password is never hashed.
rules.check: Look for new or changed password-setting paths that hash/store a password without first calling the password policy, or that call store-specific validators instead.

rules.statement: Count a password's length in Unicode code points (runes, e.g. `EnumerateRunes()`) of its NFC-normalized form, not in UTF-16 `char`s, and never truncate the password.
rules.why: NIST SP 800-63B-4 counts each Unicode code point as one character, so a surrogate pair is one character, and truncation weakens the password.
rules.check: Flag password length checks using `.Length` on a string/span, or code that truncates or substrings a password before validation or hashing.

rules.statement: Do not impose password composition rules (required digits, upper-case, symbols or other character classes).
rules.why: NIST forbids composition rules because they lead users to predictable substitutions.
rules.check: Flag password validation that requires character classes, including enabling ASP.NET Core Identity's default `PasswordOptions` requirements.

rules.statement: Require a password minimum length of at least 8 code points (15 by default for a single-factor password) and permit a maximum length of at least 64 code points.
rules.why: NIST SP 800-63B-4 requires 15 characters for a password that is the only factor, 8 as the absolute floor, and a permitted maximum of at least 64.
rules.check: Check password length settings, defaults and their validated ranges for a minimum below 8, a single-factor default below 15, or a maximum below 64.

rules.statement: Check the whole password against blocklists of common and compromised passwords and of the account's own names (user name, email, email local part), case-insensitively, and refuse it with a reason that names the requirement.
rules.why: NIST requires a blocklist comparison of the whole password and that the verifier give the reason when it refuses one; length alone lets common long passwords through.
rules.check: Flag password validation that skips blocklist checks, matches partial strings instead of the whole password, or returns a refusal without an error code and description naming the requirement.

rules.statement: Do not call a network breached-password service by default from password validation; offer it only as an opt-in extra blocklist registered by the deployment.
rules.why: A default network call makes every password change depend on a third party's availability and needs a privacy review.
rules.check: Flag default password policy or blocklist registrations that make HTTP calls.

rules.statement: Register strategy-collection implementations such as password blocklists with `TryAddEnumerable`, and register default implementations so that a host can replace them.
rules.why: The policy asks every registered blocklist in registration order, and a host must be able to add or replace them from the composition root.
rules.check: Look for blocklist or similar strategy registrations using `AddSingleton`/`AddTransient` instead of `TryAddEnumerable`, or defaults registered in a way that cannot be replaced.

rules.statement: Treat password policy error codes as an open vocabulary: consumers must handle unknown codes rather than assuming only the built-in ones exist.
rules.why: A replacement policy may report codes of its own.
rules.check: Flag exhaustive switches or mappings of policy error codes that have no fallback for unknown codes.

rules.statement: In a self-service password change, judge the new password against the policy before verifying the current password.
rules.why: The ADR orders the check so a refused new password is reported first, and a refused password is never hashed.
rules.check: In password-change flows, check that policy validation of the new password happens before verifying the current password.

rules.statement: When a seeder or other non-interactive path finds that a configured password is refused, throw an `InvalidOperationException` that names the account kind, its user name and the policy's description, instead of silently skipping or storing it.
rules.why: Seeded accounts must meet the same policy, and the failure must say which account broke which requirement.
rules.check: Flag seeding code that adds accounts without validating their passwords, or that swallows refusals.
